headline: Bitcoin is holding just above $80,000 after Wednesday's short squeeze, while Binance cut off a third-party trading tool's API keys as the fallout from last week's hack continues.

stories.title: Bitcoin holds just above $80,000 after a short squeeze and the first ETF inflow in four days
stories.summary: Bitcoin is holding above $80,000 after Wednesday's jump, which came mostly from traders who had bet on falling prices being forced to buy back. US spot bitcoin ETFs took in $74.6M on 4 November after three days of outflows, but the flows were split: Fidelity's fund took in money while BlackRock's IBIT lost money.
points: Bitcoin was about $80,250 at 11:30 UTC on 5 Nov, up about 2.5% over 24 hours, and ether was up about 4%, per CoinDesk.
Net ETF flows on 4 Nov were +$74.6M: Fidelity's FBTC +$236.7M, BlackRock's IBIT -$201.2M, per crypto.news. The three days of outflows before that added up to about $1.16B.
About $378M of bets on falling prices were liquidated in one hour, per crypto.news; CoinDesk puts liquidations across crypto at about $715M over 24 hours, about 65% of them short bets.
Bitcoin's 24-hour range was about $77,949 to $81,004, after a dip to about $75,600 during the 3 Nov election count, per crypto.news.

stories.title: Binance revokes a trading tool's API keys as it works through the fallout from its record hack
stories.summary: On 5 November Binance revoked API keys linked to SignalPlus, a third-party trading tool, after SignalPlus reported a possible security issue; Binance says its own systems and customer funds are not affected. This comes a week after the 29 October theft. A proposal to hard-fork Polygon and return a small slice of the stolen funds is up for discussion at 14:30 UTC today. For ordinary users, the lesson is that any outside tool connected to an exchange account is a possible way in.
points: About $6.34B was affected and about $2.85B has been frozen or intercepted, per crypto.news.
Binance has replenished about 98% of the affected holdings, per crypto.news.
The Polygon fork would return 70.49M POL (about $6.8M): 46.63M POL to Binance and 23.86M POL to Polymarket, per Cointelegraph.
The Polygon proposal is discussed at 14:30 UTC on 5 Nov; if approved, developers would need about two weeks of work and testing, per crypto.news's Polygon report.

stories.title: After the Democratic sweep, crypto's path in Washington gets harder
stories.summary: Democrats are set to control both chambers of Congress. House Democrats are reportedly discussing their own crypto market-structure bill that would give the SEC more responsibility and narrow the CFTC's role; no bill has been introduced. The industry group Digital Chamber called Sherrod Brown's Senate win in Ohio the most consequential unfavorable result for crypto.
points: Crypto PACs spent more than $63M backing Brown's opponent, Jon Husted, per the Digital Chamber, as reported by The Block.
The Digital Chamber still sees openings on tax reporting, custody, stablecoin implementation and consumer asset segregation (keeping customer assets separate), per The Block.
The TRUMP memecoin fell about 14% and WLFI about 4% over 24 hours, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Trump Media moves 4,259 BTC to Crypto.com
briefs.summary: About 4,259 BTC, roughly 30% of the 14,139 BTC the company reported holding on 31 July, moved to Crypto.com on 5 Nov; a move is not proof of a sale, and noteholders can demand repayment of about $1B on 30 Nov, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Arkansas sues Kalshi
briefs.summary: Arkansas's attorney general sued the prediction market, calling it illegal gambling, about a week after Utah filed criminal charges against Kalshi, per The Block.

briefs.title: French bank hit by a cyberattack that ended in crypto
briefs.summary: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirmed a cyberattack in which fraudulent transfers were converted into crypto; ZachXBT puts losses above $133M, per The Block.
